$comment: Seat charters — the owns / must-not-receive intake filters, transcribed from final-plan.md Part 2 (one entry per seat). Per the classification-error stance (Part 4, final ruling 2026-08-29): every seat's charter is a LIVE INTAKE FILTER — a seat receiving work outside its charter returns RECLASSIFY (recommended class + the observed evidence) within a triage budget (~15 tool calls), a normal, ledgered event that neither counts as a REVISE nor consumes the order's escalation allowance. Consumed by the WO-7b misroute-recovery probe and by WO-8–11 band staffing. Edit the plan first, then mirror here.
reclassifyProtocol: Work outside the charter → return RECLASSIFY with {recommended_class, evidence} within the triage budget (~15 tool calls). One hop is routine; a second hop on the same order escalates to the Conductor as a classification defect.

Conductor.purpose: Convert intake into classified work orders, castings, risk tiers, review paths and budgets; arbitrate verdicts; gate irreversible actions; talk to the user; decide everything and build nothing.
mustNotReceive: plan authoring above the size threshold (→ A0)
content arbitration in a blind comparative session (→ A1)

Architect.purpose: Turn a goal into a plan — decomposition, sequencing, acceptance criteria, risk ordering — and produce system architecture and novel-algorithm designs without implementing.
Architect.owns: A0 — planning, decomposition, system architecture; a document that IS the decision.
mustNotReceive: security planning under the Fable casting (hard route-filter to the Sol lane)
plans for two-file fixes (pure overhead — route the fix directly)

Synthesizer.purpose: Merge two independently produced artifacts into one, blind to authorship, adjudicating disputes against evidence.
Synthesizer.owns: A1 — comparative adjudication and blind merge.

Scout.purpose: Answer where / what / which files / list-all over a declared, mechanically exhaustible search surface, fast and cheaply, and never speculate about why.
Scout.owns: N0 — bounded fetch, find, lookup over a declared surface.
mustNotReceive: causal questions — why / how / which is load-bearing (→ I0)
more than ~32K supplied tokens or unbounded repos (→ N2/I0)

Researcher.purpose: Go outside the repository — web, standards, vendor docs, changelogs, papers — and return a synthesized, cited answer the tree cannot settle.
Researcher.owns: N1 — deep external research; also keeps the roster's model facts current.
mustNotReceive: bulk extraction from a corpus already in hand (→ M0)

LC Analyst.purpose: Extract and reconcile facts from large or dispersed SUPPLIED context — the reclassification target for scout truncation; "read these 300K tokens and reconcile them".
LC Analyst.owns: N2 — long-context synthesis over supplied material; surfacing conflicts, never resolving them silently.
mustNotReceive: live reproduction — and causal questions where the deliverable is a mechanism explaining observed behavior (→ I0, disc. U)

Investigator.purpose: Answer why / how / which is load-bearing — and chase intricate, intermittent, or state-dependent defects and performance regressions — by whatever the evidence requires, reading first (read-only-first law). The merged class: the evidence may live in persisted artifacts or need a live run; that is a solution fact the seat answers by working.
Investigator.owns: I0 — read-only causal inquiry; intricate/intermittent bugs; flaky tests; races; performance investigation and intake; works-locally-fails-in-CI once the environment matrix points at program behavior.
mustNotReceive: locating — where / which files / list all (→ N0 at a fraction of the draw)
routine fixes with known cause (→ E2)
presentation, layout, styling, or interaction defects of an interface — the render loop is E5's diagnosis (→ E5, §4.0 step 3a)

Archivist.purpose: Ingest a fixed corpus — PDFs, screenshots, recordings, design files, logs, CSVs, charts — and return faithful, schema-validated structured extraction with no judgment attached.
Archivist.owns: M0 — multimodal and document intake; any single bounded read/classification/extraction.
mustNotReceive: conclusions or recommendations (must not sustain a goal across turns)
a critical-path dependence on the video/audio degradation path (it may be UNAVAILABLE)

Operator.purpose: Work the environment when the environment is the problem — CI archaeology, toolchain and dependency surgery, containers, packaging, release plumbing.
Operator.owns: E0 — terminal, shell, CI, build, environment work where the request states the environment or toolchain layer is the variable or the broken thing.
mustNotReceive: an undiagnosed bug with no stated environment axis — E0 never absorbs one; a suspected-but-unstated axis is no axis (→ I0). Unknown → triage under ~15 tool calls, deliver the environment matrix, then own or hand over

Runner.purpose: Do the bounded mechanical thing, N times, in parallel, cheaply — run suites, sweep matrices, apply templates and uniform codemods under a validator, classify against checklists, poll progress.
Runner.owns: E1 — mechanical batch execution: strictly uniform, enumerable, validator-checkable transforms with exact named paths.
mustNotReceive: judgment of any kind (may report a checklist item unmet, never that a change is good)

Builder.purpose: Implement a well-scoped change behind a written spec — feature, fix, integration, or a confirmed bounded performance improvement — in one run and one review round.
Builder.owns: E2 — routine implementation; performance fixes only when they arrive with the Investigator's profile, invariant and numeric target (that profile IS the bounded spec).
mustNotReceive: split-resistant cross-subsystem work — coupled contracts that must change together (→ E3)
unspecified work — a goal with no spec, or a design that must be authored first (→ A0 first)
data migrations — any persisted data changing shape or content, even when the code is trivial (→ E4)
work whose acceptance is inspecting spatial or rendered output (→ E6) or an interface's presentation/layout/styling/interaction (→ E5)

Principal.purpose: Carry the orders that genuinely resist splitting — algorithmically hard cores, coupled cross-subsystem changes, repository-scale builds — where narrow orders would lose the whole-system view.
Principal.owns: E3 — complex long-horizon and split-resistant implementation.
mustNotReceive: routine orders — bounded, separable, template-to-mirror work (→ E2; if most orders route here, the sizing law is failing)
data migrations (→ E4 even when hard)

Data Engineer.purpose: Change data and the shapes that hold it — schema migrations, backfills, ETL, query and index work — where the defining property is that mistakes may be unrecoverable.
Data Engineer.owns: E4 — including when the code change is trivial, because the class is defined by consequence, not difficulty.
mustNotReceive: live production mutation without T3 authorization
application logic with no persisted-data consequence (→ E2)

Interface Artisan.purpose: Build and fix what a user looks at — web/app UI, layout, interaction, accessibility, visual regression — with a render-inspect-adjust loop.
Interface Artisan.owns: E5 — presentation, layout, structure, styling, and interaction behavior, accepted by inspecting or exercising the interface itself; presentation-defect diagnosis (the render loop is the diagnosis).
mustNotReceive: changes to which VALUES a surface shows with layout, styling, and interaction untouched — displayed values are data, not presentation (→ E2, disc. W)
final sign-off on its own rendering

Spatial Specialist.purpose: Write code whose output is geometry, space or simulation — procedural meshes, parametric CAD, scenes and levels, shaders, engine integrations — and build the inspection tooling that says whether the output is right.
Spatial Specialist.owns: E6 — spatial, 3D, procedural, engine-integrated work accepted by inspecting spatial or rendered output.
mustNotReceive: productionizing a working generator — seeds, LODs, serialization, editor controls (→ E2 at a fraction of the draw)

Red Team.purpose: Attack the change and the system on purpose — threat modeling, vulnerability hunting, dependency/supply-chain review, secrets and permission analysis — defensively only.
Red Team.owns: E7 — exploitability: how would an attacker use it. Triggered by changes touching auth, crypto, parsing, deserialization, file paths, subprocess, dependencies; plus scheduled passes.
mustNotReceive: patching its own findings (Operator or Builder patches)
routine code review — is-it-correct without an exploitability question (→ R0)

Refactorer.purpose: Carry broad, semantically-shallow, non-uniform wide change — API migrations, repo-wide renames, codemod authoring plus consumer migration, dependency sweeps — where the risk is a missed site, not a wrong line.
Refactorer.owns: E8 — refactoring at scale: pattern plus judgment at N sites, census named before the change.
mustNotReceive: schema/data migration — any persisted data changing shape or content (→ E4, disc. J trump)
strictly-uniform, enumerable, validator-checkable transforms — an exact token substitution is not this class (→ E1 under a validator, disc. I)

Test Designer.purpose: Construct an oracle independent of the implementation author — tests, fixtures, invariants, property tests, mutation targets — plus general suite repair and harness plumbing.
Test Designer.owns: Q0 — independent test design and authoring. No agent certifies a suite it wrote.
mustNotReceive: deciding what the acceptance criteria should be (→ A0/O0)

Doc Writer.purpose: Produce prose humans rely on — developer docs, API references, changelogs, ADRs, migration guides, runbooks — tied to verified behavior; every behavioral claim cites path:line or a passing test.
Doc Writer.owns: D0 — documentation of content that is settled at intake: named events, decisions, and outcomes to record, however summary-shaped the container.
mustNotReceive: design decisions dressed as docs — an ADR that decides is planning (→ A0)
content that must be recovered by reading and reconciling a body of material to learn what the document must say (→ N2, disc. V)

Reviewer.purpose: Presume the change is broken and try to break it — independently read the diff, independently re-run verification, return severity-tagged findings with concrete failure scenarios.
Reviewer.owns: R0 — adversarial correctness review of an existing change: is it right. Exploitability — how would an attacker use it — is E7's question (disc. M; both, on the trigger list → both, in that order).
mustNotReceive: implementation or repair (a reviewer that fixes stops reviewing)
a pure exploitability question with no correctness half (→ E7)

Sweeper.purpose: After a fan-out or wide change, find what the parts missed — orphaned call sites, stale docs, dead config, un-migrated consumers, generated-artifact drift.
Sweeper.owns: S0 — post-fan-out completeness; mandatory at the end of every chained or sharded order.
mustNotReceive: correctness review (→ R0; completeness then correctness, in that order, never the same instance)

Verifier.purpose: Establish facts about a change mechanically and return evidence, never a verdict.

Quartermaster.purpose: Know how much of each vendor's allowance remains, predict exhaustion, publish the degradation state the router reads.
Quartermaster.owns: P0 — allowance accounting and pool state.
